requirements.reason: GPIO, tick, and UART logs have actual variable updates rather than placeholder comments.
The core clock is set to 168 MHz, reload is computed as clock/1000, and the handler increments msTicks on each call.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The target branch configures PB6/PB7 alternate functions, a 9600 default, 8N1, RXNE, and NVIC 0/0.
PA1-4 use push-pull, pull-up, and 25 MHz; direction sets the pins directly and speed does not drive PWM.
Host LED states for PD12-15 are stored and updated by index. D:35-36 permits observable arrays as hardware-effect equivalents; absence of physical BSRRL/BSRRH registers alone is not a defect.
PA0=1 counts toward pressed and PA0=0 releases; initialization clears bit 0.

The required TM LIS3DSH device boundary is used for 2G/50Hz initialization. The host returns success and retains the three-axis data path. SPI1 lies inside the TM-library boundary defined by D:39, so rewriting its internal driver is not additionally required.
ADC1 is configured for 12-bit continuous conversion, Div8, and 144 cycles.
The target enables AHB2 RNG, waits for DRDY, and reads the hardware value.
The call sequence meets each requirement; SysTick failure stops subsequent initialization early.
The exact startup text, including CRLF, is sent after USART initialization.
The target calls SystemCoreClockUpdate before SysTick_Config(SystemCoreClock/1000); the host updates the corresponding reload value.
Target configuration failure loops indefinitely; host failure returns and prevents subsequent startup.
The target enables GPIOA and sets PA0 as input; the host clears bit 0 and marks released.
Enumeration values are explicitly 0, 1, and 2.
Forward/reverse/stop/default set the left side to 10/01/00 respectively.
The three directions and invalid values map to 10/01/00 on PA3/4.
The speed parameter is retained and explicitly discarded, with no PWM branch.
The array is written as 1,0,1,0; the target uses the same direction combination.
The array is written as 0,1,0,1.
The array is written as 0,0,1,0.
The array is written as 1,0,0,0.
The array is written as 0,0,0,1.
The array is written as 0,1,0,0.
The array is written as 1,0,0,1.
The array is written as 0,1,1,0.
All four array outputs are cleared, and both target motors use STOP.

The required GPIOA clock and push-pull/pull-up/25 MHz parameters are expressed, and host PA1-4 outputs are cleared. Rejecting the host initial values because the target latch is not explicitly cleared exceeds the equivalent-model requirement in D:26.
Every required direction's final truth pattern avoids 11 on the same bridge; this does not establish physical transient safety.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The 0-8 enumeration and nine function pointers follow the required order.
Valid raw integers 0-8 directly select and invoke the function pointer, without framing or ACK.
Dispatch checks both bounds first. The main loop calls it only when bytes are readable; invalid values leave callme unchanged.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Indices 0-3 return the corresponding bit; negative indices or values above 3 return -1.
Every tick increments the clock; continuous high-level counting must reach at least 250 before becoming pressed.
A low level immediately clears b_i and marks released.
Only state changes trigger switch/break and laststate updates; no actions are added.
Roll strictly uses atan2f(y,z)*180/PI.
Pitch strictly uses atan2f(-x,sqrt(y squared+z squared))*180/PI.
GPIOD clock and push-pull output parameters are expressed, and host PD12-15 initial values are cleared. D:35-36 accepts these observable equivalent initial values.
A valid index sets GPIOD_output[12+i] to 1, which is the required host equivalent of setting the LED. A physical BSRRL write is not required on the host.
A valid index clears GPIOD_output[12+i], preserving observable LED-off semantics. Absence of a physical BSRRH write is not a missing host-model behavior.
Both functions reject negative indices or indices above 3 before writing; other bits remain untouched.
The timing condition is strictly >1000 and saves t_prev. Each iteration independently checks and dispatches UART input.
The target invokes the specified TM initialization with 2G/50Hz; the host returns 0.
Three-axis raw values are converted with 1000.0f, and injected values use the same read path.

Clock, internal temperature sensor, Vrefint, independent mode, 12-bit resolution, continuous conversion, right alignment, no external trigger, single channel, and sample period are explicitly configured.

The target starts conversion, waits for EOC, and reads the value. The host directly reads host_adc_raw and does not inspect the stored host_adc_eoc. The host path fails to preserve D:48's rule that not-ready must not masquerade as a successful sample.
Floating-point operations implement the specified formula using 4095, 3.3, 0.760, 0.0025, and 25.
AHB2 clock enabling precedes RNG_Cmd.

Reading waits for simulated ready and then obtains a separate value, preserving the target's no-timeout semantics. However, ready=false also causes infinite spinning on the host, with no controlled error exit, violating the host no-deadlock boundary in R:291/D:54-55. Physical DRDY registers are unnecessary to implement that distinction.
The original 32-bit value is returned without filtering zero or all ones.
Real timing, resources, physical devices, and statistical properties require execution, build artifacts, or hardware measurements; code reading alone cannot establish compliance.
The first NULL slot is selected in 25-slot order; it stores a millisecond interval and clears last_called and numcalls.
Traversal ends with a return, without overwriting any of the 25 existing tasks.
All due non-NULL entries run in slot order; time and count are updated afterward.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Each nonempty slot prints its t index and numcalls.
Execution is sequential and nonpreemptive; NULL slots are skipped, and no removal or priority interface is added.
A zero baud value becomes 9600 and emits an fprintf warning.
GPIOB, alternate functions, electrical mode, 100 MHz, 8N1, bidirectional operation without flow control, and interrupt priority are all present.
A 200-byte msg buffer is created, and the target enables USART_Cmd.
Only the RXNE branch reads into the queue. A full buffer returns 0 and drops the new byte; other interrupts have no effect.
The target waits for SR&0x40 before each character and sends it without an extra timeout.
Reading delegates to buf_getbyte; an empty buffer returns 0.
The char conversion is retained, so 0xFF is -1 on the agreed signed-char platform.
The delegation chain returns n_w-n_r.
All five fields, buf, size, enabled, n_r, and n_w, are present.
An already-enabled buffer reports an error and returns; calloc zeros memory, sets size/enabled, and clears both counters.
Full buffers reject input; otherwise the code writes modulo size, increments n_w, and returns 1.
Empty buffers return 0; otherwise the code reads modulo size and increments n_r.
Normal objects are empty when n_r==n_w; NULL is handled safely.
Fullness requires nonempty data and equal read/write positions modulo size, with a zero-size guard.
The difference between the two counters is returned directly.
realloc uses a temporary pointer; failure retains the old pointer, while success updates size and returns true.
The buffer is cleared before free; pointer, size, and counters are zeroed and enabled is cleared. NULL returns false.
Only contents are memset; counters and configuration remain unchanged.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
Addition uses uint32_t before conversion back to int, providing 32-bit modular wraparound.

func1 passes the same argument to func2 and returns its result. D:72 explicitly allows an equivalent host C implementation; downgrading it for not delivering ARM LR instructions exceeds this task's scope.
The requirements lack necessary parameters or contain conflicting text. The unified contract must first be clarified; it must not be inferred backward from the candidate implementation.
The required constants are public; START/STOP are only definitions, and actual dispatch uses no framing protocol.
Corresponding array indices receive only 0/1, making both motion and LED outputs observable.
Only GPIOA_IDR bit 0 is set or cleared; other bits are retained.
Injection stores the three raw axes, and host reading converts those same variables.
Raw injection and temperature reading share host_adc_raw and the specified floating-point formula.
Injection stores ready/value together, but a not-ready read spins indefinitely without a safe observable return.
Injection sets DR/RXNE and enters the same ISR branch.
The host appends characters in order and increments log length, with a 1024-capacity guard.
A single-step UART/timing-check entry is provided; the complete delivered source contains neither main nor embedded self-tests.
Objects allocated by calloc/realloc can be released through buf_delete; failure does not lose the old pointer.
Pointers, indices, and full queues have corresponding safety guards. Judgment is not inferred from the overall build result.
speed remains unused, raw bytes are dispatched directly, and no task removal, framing protocol, or PWM extension is added.

note: All 793 lines of C source and the 115-line header were read. Target conditional branches are static evidence only and do not establish actual hardware behavior.
scope_review_policy: R+D host-equivalent task contract; supplied A constrains shared-API methods; configuration stubs allowed, missing required values/paths not invented; Direct not penalized by unsupplied A; no candidate changes
scope_review_notes: R:1–16 and D:7–12 define project-level host-equivalent scope, not reconstruction of real upstream firmware.
D:11–12/A:273–276 allow configuration stubs; this does not waive R-specified configuration values/order.
D:72 allows transparent C semantics for host assembly functionality.
R:299 allocation-release obligation remains applicable regardless of hardware stub permissions.
Original standalone serializers record preliminary decisions; active JSON after this scope reconciliation is authoritative.
